partners.diseaseBName: deafness, cataract, impaired intellectual development, and polyneuropathy
partners.mechanism_chain: CDH11 (HGNC:2342) —DISRUPTS→ Cell adhesion and migration (GO:0007155); Cell adhesion and migration (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); PSMC3 (HGNC:9930) —DISRUPTS→ proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital cataract (HP:0000510); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Polyneuropathy (HP:0003474); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Haploinsufficiency of CDH11 disrupts normal cell adhesion and migration processes, indirectly contributing to intellectual disability. Haploinsufficiency of PSMC3 directly impairs proteasome function, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular dysfunction, which manifests as congenital cataract, polyneuropathy, and sensorineural hearing impairment. The convergence occurs at the level of proteasome function, as PSMC3 is a core component of the proteasome, and impaired proteasome function can exacerbate cellular stress and dysfunction, potentially impacting neuronal development and function, thus linking to intellectual disability as well.

partners.diseaseBName: neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, hypotonia, and absent language
partners.mechanism_chain: CDH11 (HGNC:2358) —DISRUPTS→ Cellular adhesion and migration (GO:0007155); Cellular adhesion and migration (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial shape (HP:0000241); PSMB1 (HGNC:9704) —DISRUPTS→ Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Absent language (HP:0012754). Haploinsufficiency of CDH11 disrupts cellular adhesion and migration pathways, leading to phenotypes such as abnormal facial shape in Elsahy-Waters syndrome. #### 1. Ebstein-Bezieau neurodevelopmental syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9958825)

**Proposed mechanism:** CDH11 (HGNC:2352) —DISRUPTS→ proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0043161); PSMC3 (HGNC:9901) —DISRUPTS→ proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0043161); proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0043161) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0043161) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability, severe (HP:0010804); proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0043161) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial shape (HP:0000241); proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0043161) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defect (HP:0001627). Haploinsufficiency of CDH11 in Elsahy-Waters syndrome and PSMC3 in Ebstein-Bezieau neurodevelopmental syndrome both converge on disrupting the function of the proteasome complex. This disruption leads to a shared downstream phenotype including developmental delay, intellectual disability, abnormal facial features, and congenital heart defects.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any observed disruption to proteasome function in cellular models of CDH11 or PSMC3 haploinsufficiency, or identification of distinct molecular pathways for each disease that do not involve the proteasome. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in CDH11 or PSMC3 in the gnomAD database that are not associated with either disease would weaken the causal link for those specific variants.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying a shared mechanistic link through proteasome dysfunction could suggest therapeutic strategies targeting protein degradation pathways that might benefit patients with either Elsahy-Waters syndrome or Ebstein-Bezieau neurodevelopmental syndrome.

#### 2. deafness, cataract, impaired intellectual development, and polyneuropathy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.443)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9958825)

**Proposed mechanism:** CDH11 (HGNC:2342) —DISRUPTS→ Cell adhesion and migration (GO:0007155); Cell adhesion and migration (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); PSMC3 (HGNC:9930) —DISRUPTS→ proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital cataract (HP:0000510); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Polyneuropathy (HP:0003474); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405); proteasome-dependent protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Haploinsufficiency of CDH11 disrupts normal cell adhesion and migration processes, indirectly contributing to intellectual disability. Haploinsufficiency of PSMC3 directly impairs proteasome function, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular dysfunction, which manifests as congenital cataract, polyneuropathy, and sensorineural hearing impairment. The convergence occurs at the level of proteasome function, as PSMC3 is a core component of the proteasome, and impaired proteasome function can exacerbate cellular stress and dysfunction, potentially impacting neuronal development and function, thus linking to intellectual disability as well.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that pathogenic variants in CDH11 do not lead to haploinsufficiency, or if pathogenic variants in PSMC3 do not impair proteasome function, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, the absence of intellectual disability in individuals with PSMC3 mutations or the absence of cataracts/polyneuropathy/hearing impairment in individuals with CDH11 mutations would weaken the proposed link.

**Why it matters:** Identifying a shared mechanistic basis in protein homeostasis, specifically involving the proteasome, could open avenues for therapeutic strategies that target proteasome function or downstream consequences of its impairment, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
